summary: Iteration 4 (security audit) PASSED. Backend: 22/22 new security tests in test_security.py + 39/40 pre-existing (1 flaky test_barbers.py::test_different_barbers_same_time_both_ok caused by shared-DB state from prior runs — not security-related, pre-existing issue). SEC-001 verified visually at 390x844 AND 1366x800: login screen renders with empty email/password (both inputs return '' from input_value) and login still works for admin@wendelcortes.com/admin123 (→ /dashboard) and carlos@test.com/cliente123 (→ /home). SEC-002: /api/queue/today as carlos abbreviates other clients' names ('Carlos S.', 'João P.' etc.), strips client_phone and user_id from other entries (both top-level entries[] and queues[].entries[]); own entry keeps full phone + user_id; admin sees full entries including phone. Client Fila screen highlights own entry via entry.id now (fila.tsx:130 `e.id === data.my_entry?.id` ✓). SEC-003: tokens signed with 'dev-secret' or any wrong secret → 401 on /auth/me; new tokens accepted; decoded exp-iat ≈ 7 days (within 1h window). SEC-004: POST /seed without token → 401; with carlos token → 403; with admin token → 200; services count stayed 7 and barbers count unchanged before/after (idempotent). SEC-005: POST /appointments with date 'xx' → 400, time '25:99' → 400 (both now return proper 400 via parse_date_or_400 / validate_time_or_400, previously 500); POST /barbers/{id}/blocks with bad date or time → 422 (pydantic regex); PUT /barbers/{id} with work_hours.start='abc' → 422; GET /barbers/available/not-a-date → 400; GET /barbers/schedule/bad → 400. Hardening: register with password 'abc' → 400 'A senha deve ter pelo menos 6 caracteres'; register with existing email → 400 with neutral message ('Não foi possível criar a conta…') — explicitly asserted NOT to contain 'já cadastrado'; POST /register-push without token → 401; CORS preflight for Origin https://evil.example returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin '*' and does NOT set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (allow_credentials=False when CORS_ORIGINS='*' — correct). Rate limit: 10 consecutive wrong-password attempts for a throwaway email returned 401, 11th returned 429 (backend was restarted after each pytest run to clear the in-memory failure dict so subsequent frontend/login tests weren't blocked). Frontend smoke: carlos booking flow (services list shows all 7, 'Qualquer' barber picker tappable), admin dashboard loads at 1366x800 showing R$225.00 faturamento / 7 agendamentos / 5 concluídos / 9 na fila / 4 mensalistas and the Fila do João panel with full client phones (admin view). Zero JS runtime errors; only innocuous expo-notifications web warnings.
action_items: (optional, non-blocking) test_barbers.py::TestPerBarberConflict::test_different_barbers_same_time_both_ok is a pre-existing flaky test caused by shared DB state across runs (Wendel 10:00 slot keeps accumulating prior TEST appointments and returns 409). Not related to this iteration's security fixes. Consider adding a cleanup fixture or picking a per-test unique date (e.g. uuid-based future date) when stabilising.

(optional) The rate-limit backing store is an in-memory dict (LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES/LOGIN_WINDOW in server.py). On multi-worker/multi-replica deployments it will be bypassed; consider Redis before scaling horizontally. Fine for the current single-worker preview env.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py JWT_SECRET validation (len<32 raises RuntimeError at import) is a strong, fail-fast guarantee — new backend/.env has a 64-char secret.

public_queue_entry() correctly strips client_phone AND user_id for others while keeping own entry intact; both the top-level entries[] and per-barber queues[].entries[] are run through it (server.py:730-735). Fila UI now matches on entry.id (not user_id, which clients no longer see for others).

parse_date_or_400 / validate_time_or_400 are used only in create_appointment; other endpoints rely on pydantic regex (DATE_RE/TIME_RE) in barbers.py — both paths return 400/422 instead of 500 which satisfies SEC-005.

/seed is now behind require_admin (server.py:938). Startup still auto-runs seed() which is idempotent (count/find-first guards for admin, settings, services, barbers; SEED_DEMO_DATA gate before demo clients/appointments).

Register duplicate response is a single neutral message that intentionally does NOT disclose whether the e-mail is registered — mitigates user enumeration. Weak-password check runs BEFORE the DB lookup so you can't use it as an enumeration oracle via timing.

CORS: allow_credentials=(CORS_ORIGINS != ['*']) — correctly refuses to combine credentials with wildcard origin (would otherwise be an open-CORS vulnerability). Preflight response verified: ACAO=* and no ACAC header.

Rate limit (per IP + per email, 10/15min) is applied before the password check — safe against both targeted and spray attacks. Successful login clears both counters (server.py:265). Backend restart clears state, which is acceptable for the preview environment but worth replacing with Redis for production.
frontend/.env now exposes only EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL; no admin credentials or client credentials are hardcoded in the login screen (login.tsx uses useState('')).
jwt token exp set to 7 days (server.py:65) — matches spec; iat is not set, so clients that need iat should rely on current time at decode (not critical).

success_rate.backend: 100% on security suite (22/22). Combined regression: 61/63 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing mensal cycle exhaustion), 1 failed (pre-existing flaky test unrelated to this iteration).
success_rate.frontend: 100% on smoke (login empty-state 390+1366, client login+Agendar flow, admin login+dashboard).

seed_data_creation: Several TEST_weak_*/TEST_ratelimit-test-*@x.com throwaway accounts were created by hardening tests and are harmless (they only exist in users collection with role=client). The 11-wrong-password rate-limit test runs against a fresh uuid-suffixed email so no real account is locked. Backend was restarted after each pytest invocation (which calls rate-limit test) to clear the in-memory failure dict before frontend tests ran — otherwise frontend login would 429 for 15 minutes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After running test_security.py the in-memory login failure dict will contain the test IP for 15 minutes (10+ failures recorded). ALWAYS `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` before running frontend login smoke tests when the rate-limit test has just executed, or deselect TestRateLimitLast with --deselect 'backend/tests/test_security.py::TestRateLimitLast'. Env today 2026-10-03 (Saturday, fila mode) → fila has 4+ waiting entries (seeded + leftover TEST Queue). Admin credentials unchanged: admin@wendelcortes.com / admin123; carlos@test.com / cliente123 (and joao/rafael/marcos/lucas@test.com same password). JWT_SECRET in backend/.env is a 64-char random string — do NOT replace it or old tokens will become invalid. CORS_ORIGINS env is not set so defaults to ['*'] with allow_credentials=False. Register duplicate error message is now 'Não foi possível criar a conta com estes dados. Se você já tem cadastro, faça login.' — any test asserting 'já cadastrado' will fail (none currently do).
rca_of_issue: N/A — all security fixes behave as specified. The one failing test (test_different_barbers_same_time_both_ok) is a pre-existing cross-run data accumulation issue in test_barbers.py; booking Wendel at 10:00 on 2026-10-06 is now a 409 because prior test runs already placed appointments there. Easiest fix is to use a uuid-generated future date per test (not done to stay within fix-scope).
